SHRI BALAVANT alias BAL APTE: Sir, to deal with the question of 
starvation, it needs a comprehensive policy framework, along with food, 
agriculture and farmers. Today, we find that all these aspects are 
considered in a disjointed way. Therefore, the process of planning gets 
affected. On the one hand, you tell the farmers that they need not depend 

27 
on agriculture. You want the population, depending on agriculture, to be 
reduced; on the other hand, the farmer is given, if at all, only a 
minimum price that will help him survive. There is no profit in it. He 
can't produce more. Therefore,  is  there  any policy framework in the 
mind of the Government that will deal with starvation  

28 
directly, that will give the farmers profit- making remunerations, which 
will give the agriculture the necessary priority, and where food will be 
a matter of concern? Is there any such framework in the mind of the 
Government? Is the Minister in a position to spell it out? 
SHRI SHARAD PAWAR: Sir, there are three aspects about the farmers and 
farmers' position, how to improve the productivity, and, ultimately, how 
to resolve the problem of the food security of this country. The most 
important thing is the availability of the food and production of the 
food. This Government has taken a conscious decision to provide a better 
price to the farmers. One can just see the prices that were provided for 
wheat last year. It was somewhat Rs. 1000/-  per quintal. It was, in the 
next year, raised by Rs. 300/-  per quintal. Similar is the situation in 
the case of rice, oilseeds, pulses, sugarcane, and practically each and 
every crop. Because of this farmer- friendly policy, one can see that in 
the year 2005- 06, the total production in this country was 208 million 
tonnes; in the year 2006 -07, it had gone to 217 million tonnes; and, in 
the year 2007- 08, it had gone to 230 million tonnes. So, there was 6.2 
per cent growth in the year 2007-08. This is a clear-cut indication as to 
why there was more production. It was mainly because of the proper prices 
provided to the farmers. 
Now, I come to the issue of starvation. The part 'a' of the question 
says, "Whether it is a fact that the International Food Policy Research 
Institute has stated that 23 crore people face starvation in India;". In 
fact, I tried to collect the International Food Policy Research 
Institute's report. They had published a paper in October 2008. Its 
subject is, "The India State Hunger Index– Comparison of Hunger Across 
States." The actual statement which they have made does not say that it 
is 23 crores, and, secondly, they have not mentioned that as 
'starvation'. Their statement states that there are more than 200 million 
people in India who are 'food insecure'. They have mentioned it as 'food 
insecure', and there is a difference between the 'starvation' and 'the 
food insecure'. The availability of foodgrains is there. I have to accept 
one thing that there are sizable sections in the society where the 
availability of food is there but they have a limited purchasing power 
and, therefore, they are not in a position to afford the purchase as per 
their requirement. So, I am not in a position to deny that factual 
position. That is a factual position, and, in fact, in the last year or 

29 
in the year before the last year, globally, the foodgrain prices had gone 
up like anything and that has affected the poor sections of the society, 
not only in India but also throughout the globe. The FAO had called a 
separate meeting for that purpose and taken certain actions. 
But forget about what is happening outside India. In our country with 
regard to the section which is facing the problem of food insecurity, the 
Government of India has taken many decisions and this is not only today. 
The previous Government had also taken many decisions; today's Government 
has improved upon these decisions and one can see it. If we take the case 
of IFPRI, they have said that a population of 23 crore comes under the 
category of 'food insecurity'. Sir, let us anal yse this figure of '23 
crore'. The figure of '23 crore' is not accepted by the Planning 
Commission and this figure is also not  accepted  by  the  NSSO.  But  
still I am ready to accept this for calculation purposes. They have  

30 
said that a population of 23 crore is affected. Now, to help those 
people, under the AAY, Antyodaya Anna Yojana, we are providing foodgrains 
- 35 kg per family; wheat at two rupees per kilo and rice at three rupees 
per kilo -  to 13 crore people. Under the BPL, where we are providing 
foodgrains at cheaper rate, we have covered a population of 21 crore. So, 
this figure combined together -  the number of people covered under AAY, 
BPL plus the number of people covered under the Old Age Pension, which is 
around 1.57 crore - comes to around 36 crore. The IFPRI is saying that a 
population of 23 crore is affected. So, we have already taken care of 36 
crore people and then there are some other schemes where some alternative 
arrangements have been made which has been given in detail here

Statement 
(a) No, Sir. The Details regarding import of fertilizers during the 
years 2006-07 to 2008-09 are at Statement-I (See below). 
(b) Does not arise. The requirement, availability and sales of major 
fertilizers in the country for the year 2008- 09 (April, 2008 to 
January, 2009) are at Statement-II (see below). 
(c) Urea is the only fertilizer which is under partial movement and 
distribution control of the Government. Union Government ensures 
availability of urea at State level. State Governments are responsible 
and take appropriate measures for its distribution within the State. 
(d) The steps taken by the Department of Fertilizers for smooth 
distribution of fertilizers are as under: 
 i) Movement of fertilizers is being monitored throughout the country 
by an on-line web based monitoring system to track production, 
imports, dispatch, arrival and sales up to the district level. The 
data is also accessible to public at www.urvarak.co.in 
 ii) The subsidy on fertilizers is to be paid only when it reaches the 
district; 
 iii) Department of Fertilizers operates Buffer Stock of urea in major 
urea consuming states, up to a limit of 5% of the seasonal

requirement through State Institutional Agencies / fertilizer 
companies; 
 iv) The gap between requirement and indigenous availability of Urea, 
DAP and MOP is met through imports; 
 v) Department of Fertilizers contacts the authorities of the State 
Agriculture Department everyday to find out any shortage of 
fertilizers anywhere in the state and based on the feed back 
received immediate remedial steps are taken; 

42 
 vi) Periodic Review meetings on availability of fertilizers are held 
between the Officers of the State Agriculture Department and 
fertilizer suppliers by Secretary (Fertilizer) to resolve the 
problems, if any, faced by the S tate Government / fertilizer 
suppliers. 
 vii) The Department of Fertilizers has been facilitating the State 
Governments in procurement of the decontrolled fertilizers through 
indigenous manufacturers and importers. 
 viii) Policy for uniform freight subsidy on all fertilizers 
under the fertilizer subsidy regime has been implemented from 1st 
April, 2008.

2. As is clear from the above table, the S tate of Himachal Pradesh was 
allocated total funds of Rs. 240.68 crore under NRHM out of which an 
amount of Rs. 235.80 crore has been released to it. The State has 
reported the utilisation of an total amount of Rs. 190.59 crore 
leaving an unspent balance of Rs. 45.21 crore as on 31st Dec 2008. 
During the year 2008- 09, the State was allocated an amount of Rs. 
71.03 crore out of which 53.49 crore was released. The State has 
reported utilisation of an amount of Rs. 39.89 crore as on 31st Dec 
2008. 
3. Under the National Rural Health Mission, the allocation of funds is on 
basis of the population of the respective State multiplied by the 
appropriate factor depending on whether the State is a High Focus 
State or North Eastern State etc. The State of Himachal Pradesh is a 
high focus State. Its allocation is computed by multiplying its 
population based entitlement by 1.5. Hence the higher allocation to 
the State under NRHM. 
4. Under the NRHM, release of funds to States is on basis of the Annual 
Programme Implementation Plan (PIP) which is prepared by the State and 
appraised and approved by the National Programme Coordination 
Committee at the level of the Government of India. The State has 
submitted detailed PIP during all the years under NRHM and the funds 
have been released after it is appraised and approved. The State has 
detailed plans for utilisation of the funds allocated to it for 

55 
achieving the targets of NRHM. 
5. Under the NRHM, implementation of the Annual PIP is monitored 
rigorously through a multi pronged monitoring framework. This includes 
regular visits by officials of the Government of India to the State 
for spot reviews, Review Missions, periodic MIS, Financial M anagement 
Reports, independent reviews etc. The State of Himachal Pradesh has 
substantially improved its capacity to utilize the funds which are 
released to it for rejuvenation of the health system. A large  
part  of  funds  are  blocked  in  physical  construction/ upgradation 
of public health facilities. The  

56 
construction activity is a long term activity and is spread over more 
than one year. Some of the unspent balance with the State is committed 
towards such activities. The relatively high unspent balance is 
therefore a systemic feature of the health sector reform agenda being 
undertaken under NRHM and does not necessarily reflect poor 
utilisation by the State. 
6. The Government of India supports the States to facilitate appropriate 
and accelerated utilisation of funds released u nder NRHM. For this 
purpose series of workshops have also been organised to assist the 
States and build capacity for programme planning and implementation. 
Conversion of wasteland into cultivatble land 
†*6. DR. MURLI MANOHAR JOSHI: 
 SHRI RAM JETHMALANI: 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that 17.45 per cent of land is wasteland in 
the country; 
(b) if not, the facts in this regard; 
(c) the area of wasteland which has been converted into agricultural 
land from 2006 to 2008; and 
(d) the total area of wasteland targeted to be converted into 
cultivable land during the Eleventh Five Year Plan? 
THE MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI SHARAD PAWAR): (a) to (d) As per 
Wasteland Atlas of India, 2005, of Ministry of Rural Development, 
Department of Land Resources, Government of India, the total area of 
wasteland is 55.27 million ha. which is 17.45 per cent of total 
geographical area of the country. 
Various schemes/programmes of Watershed Development are under 
implementation to develop the degraded land including wasteland with the 
objective of preventing soil erosion, land degradation, maintaining 
balance in different types of land uses, increasing moisture and 
groundwater recharge, sustaining productivity etc. It is because of these 
programmes that the Net Sown Area in the country has remained 
approximately the same i.e. 141 million ha. despite increase in area 
under non-agricultural uses over last two decades. 
Government of India has targeted an area of 32.05 million ha. for 
development of degraded land including wastelands under various watershed 
development programmes during the XI Five Year Plan.

 MS. MABEL REBELLO: 
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is proposed to provide second line treatment to HIV

THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE (DR. ANBUMANI RAMDOSS): (a) 
to (d) The Government of India announced the provision of second line 
Anti-retroviral Treatment (ART) on 1st December, 2007 for patients who 
develop resistance to first-line ART. It was rolled out on pilot basis at 
two centres viz. J.J. Hospital, Mumbai and GHTM, Tambaram, from 1st 
January, 2008. Based on the experience gained in the pilot study, the 
second line ART has been initiated in eight more hospitals, namely Gandhi 
Hospital, Hyderabad; PGIMER, Chandigarh; Maulana Azad Medical College, 
New Delhi; B.J. Medical College, Ahmedabad; Bowring and Lady Curzon 
Hospital, Bangalore; RIMS, Imphal; School of Tropical Medicine, Kolkata 
and Institute of Medical Sciences, BHU, Varanasi. Capacities have since 
been developed in these institutes by way of trained doctors and 
laboratory facilities required for initiating and monitoring second line 
ART. Second-line ART shall be provided free of cost to eligible patients 
below poverty line (BPL), widows & children and to patients under 

67 
treatment in Government ART centers continuously for at least two years, 
irrespective of income status. 
As facilities for investigations required for determining drug 
resistant cases are limited, second- line ART is being rolled out in a 
phased manner to enable the institutions to gain required expertise and 
experience. Accordingly the institutions will, in the first phase, cover 
eligible patients from their own  centre  followed  by  expanding  
services to other States linked to them. Patients from Bihar and

Allocation of foodgrains to Uttarakhand 
†*15. SHRI BHAGAT SINGH KOSHYARI: Will the Minister of CONSUMER 
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that allocation of foodgrains under Public 
Distribution System to the State of Uttarakhand has been reduced during  
the last two years; 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 

76 
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and 
(c) whether the number of poor families in the State of Uttarakhand is 
less than national average and whether any scheme is under consideration 
with Government to allocate more foodgrains to such States under the 
Public Distribution System? 
THE MINISTER OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (SHRI 
SHARAD PAWAR): (a) and (b) No, Sir. There has not been any reduction in 
last two years in the allocations of food grains to Uttarakhand for BPL 
and AAY ration card holders under Targeted Public Distribution System 
(TPDS). As per allocation norms, allocations of food grains under TPDS 
are made @ 35 kg per family per month for all accepted numbers of BPL and 
AAY families for all the States/UTs, including the State of Uttarakhand. 
This norm is based on 1993- 94 poverty estimates of the Planning 
Commission and population estimates of Registrar General of India, as on 
1.3.2000 or the number of families actually identified and ration cards 
issued by States/UTs, whichever is less. 
Allocations of food grains for the Above Poverty Line (APL) families 
are made depending upon availability of food grains in the Central Pool. 
Because of shortage of food grains in the Central Pool during 2006-07 and 
2007-08, it was decided from June 2006 and April 2007 to base allocations 
on offtake during the earlier three years. This was done to limit 
allocations within the stocks available in the Central Pool. 
(c) As per 1993-94 poverty estimates of Planning Commission, 40.85% of 
population in Uttarakhand was living below poverty line. The national 
level of population below poverty line during 1993-94 was 36%. Since full 
allocations of food grains under TPDS are being made to the State as per 
allocation norms for all accepted numbers of BPL families, there is no 
proposal to further increase BPL/AAY allocations. 
Herbal cure from malaria 
*16. SHRI N.K. SINGH: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that a plant named Gonmostama found in the 
North Eastern part of the country has been found to be an effective cure 
against malaria; 
(b) whether Government plans to conduct further research on the 
effectiveness of the plant for curing malaria; and 
(c) if so, the details in this regard? 

77 
THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE (DR. ANBUMANI RAMDOSS): (a) 
to (c) Yes Sir, Defence Research Laboratory (DRL), Tezpur, Defence 
Research and Development Organization (DRDO) under Ministry of Defence 
has identified two species of Gomphostema, which have the potential cure 
both types of Malaria i.e. Plasmodhim vivax & Plasmodium falciparum. Both 
the plant species are abundantly available in the Foothills of Assam & 
Arunachal Pradesh border. DRL Tejpur carried out preliminary research 
with the crude extract of the subject plant i.e.  Gomphostema and the in-
vitro tests with the same was found to be effective against strains of 
Plasmodium falciparum. Encouraged by the results in the preliminary 
studies, DRDO is currently undertaking advanced research with the plant  
i.e. isolation and characterization of the active compound which is 
expected to improve the efficacy against Malaria.

Bio-technology for agriculture 
3. DR. K. MALAISAMY: Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether India will be a leading country in 2020 in producing GM 
rice, wheat, vegetables by using bio- technology instead of conventional 
practices; 
(b) the details of the move proposed towards this end; and 
(c) what could be the adverse effect of soil by resorting to bio-
technology and in using the products through bio-technology means? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI KANTILAL 
BHURIA): (a) and (b) India considers biotechnology as a powerful tool in 
breaking breeding barriers. Accordingly, a special project on 
‘Transgenics in Crops' covering 14 crops, including rice and vegetables, 
has been undertaken. India continuous to strive for harnessing the 
benefits of biotechnology in conjunction with conventional tools, 
specially for managing various biotic and abiotic stresses and quality 
improvement. 
(c) GM crops are released for commercial cultivation only after 
assessing the risk including that on soil, and after being satisfied 
about their safety in all respects.

5. DR. GYAN PRAKASH PILANIA: Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether India produces nearly 11.90 per cent and 10.90 per cent of 
world production of vegetables and fruits, respectively, while its share 
in the global market in vegetables and fruits stand at 1.70 per cent and 
0.50 per cent, respectively; 
(b) if so, reasons for such poor performance, remedial steps taken and 
outcome thereof; 
(c) how much of fruits/vegetables go waste, due to lack of proper 
storage etc.; 
(d) whether the Indian farmers receive less than a fifth of the high 
price that the consumer pays and the lion's share is usurped by 
middlemen; and 

102 
(e) if so, how pathetic is plight of farmer? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI KANTILAL 
BHURIA): (a) and (b) India produces 13 per cent and 12 per cent of world 
production of vegetables and fruits respectively and its share in the 
global market is about 1.38 per cent in respect of vegetables & fruits. 
India is the 2nd largest producer of vegetables and fruits and this 
Ministry aims at doubling the production of fruits and vegetables by 
2011-12. For this several schemes have been implemented since 2005- 06. 
There is an increase of 15 per cent in vegetable production and 8 percent 
in fruit production by the end of 2007-08. 

103 
(c) About 10-30 per cent of fruits and vegetables go waste due to poor 
handling and lack of post harvest management. 
(d) and (e) No survey has yet been conducted on net share received by 
farmers out of consumers payment and no authentic data is available.

Compensation to farmers affected due to snow fall 
†7. SHRI LALIT KISHORE CHATURVEDI: Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) the details of crop losses due to long severe winter as a result 
of snow fall, frost and fog in northern India during January- February, 
2008. State-wise; 
(b) the details of financial assistance provided to affected fanners 
by Government, State-wise; 
(c) whether Government is contemplating to include frost, fog etc. in 
natural calamity; 
(d) whether State Governments are authorized to utilize C.R.F. to 
extend relief to the affected farmers; and 

104 
(e) if not, whether Government would give its permission? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI KANTILAL 
BHURIA): (a) to (e) There are two schemes for providing assistance to the 
States towards immediate relief in the wake of natural calamities viz. 
Calamity Relief Fund (CRF) and National Calamity Contingency Fund (NCCF). 
The types of calamities, for which the States are eligible for assistance 
under the  
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 

105 
schemes are determined by the successive Finance Commissions set up from 
time - to - time. The Twelfth Finance Commission has not considered Cold 
Wave/Frost/Fog/Snowfall etc. as calamities qualifying for assistance from 
CRF & NCCF. Under the circumstances the State Governments, who are 
primarily responsible for taking immediate measures in the wake of 
natural calamities, are required to meet the expenditure on such events 
from their own resources. The eligible farmers are, however, entitled for 
compensation under the National Agricultural Insurance Scheme (NAIS) of 
the Ministry of Agriculture, subject to certain conditions being 
fulfilled by the respective State Governments. Peril-wise loss assessment 
under NAIS is not made. It is a multi- peril, yield-based Crop Insurance 
Scheme, under which yield loss is compensated to a certain extent.

Production of pulses 
†9. SHRI LALIT KISHORE CHATURVEDI: Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) the total area in the country in which pulses are generally sown; 
(b) the estimated area in which pulses have been sown in the Kharif 
season during 2008-09; 
(c) whether it is a fact that pulses have been sown in only 65 per 
cent of the area this year which would result in a reduction of a minimum 
of 10 lac tonnes of production in pulses; 
(d) whether it is a fact that pulses sector has been neglected in 
green revolution and their production continues to remain at subsistence 
level; and 
(e) whether any scheme is under consideration to meet this shortage? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI KANTILAL 
BHURIA): (a) The Normal area under pulses is 224.60 lakh ha including 
Kharif, Rabi and Summer. 
(b) and (c) The area under pulses during Kharif season of 2008- 09 is 
estimated at 88.44 lakh hectare which is 81.42% of normal Kharif area. 

111 
However, prolonged rainy season in Kharif has brightened prospects of 
increased production of Rabi pulses. The contribution of Kharif and 
Rabi/Summer seasons to t he normal production of pulses is 37% and 63% 
respectively. 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 

112 
(d) The production of pulses has increased from 83.50 lakh tonnes in 
1966-67 to 151.12 lakh tonnes in 2007-08. 
(e) Government of India is implementing various schemes to encourage 
cultivation of pulses as given below: 
1. Integrated Scheme of Oilseeds, Pulses, Oil Palm and Maize (ISOPOM) in 
14 major pulses growing State. 
2. National Food Security Mission- Pulses launched in 2007- 08 being 
implemented in 171 identified district of 14 major pulses growing 
States with objective to enhance production of pulses by 20.00 lakh 
tonnes by the 11th Five Year Plan. 
3. Macro Management of Agriculture (MMA) Scheme which provides assistance 
to the States not covered under ISOPOM. 
4. Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY) under which States can undertake 
Pulse Development Programme. 
New farming practice in Tamil Nadu 
10. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR SANGHI: Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether a new farming practice has been developed in Tamil Nadu to 
increase the productivity of land, water and other farm inputs in 
cultivation of Rice Crops; 
(b) if so, has this practice incorporated some innovative features 
over the conventional way of flooded rice cultivation; and 
(c) whether the existing problems like water- scarcity, high energy 
usage and environmental degradation would adequately be taken care of and 
thus crop yield is substantially increased? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI KANTILAL 
BHURIA): (a) to (c) The System of Rice Intensification (SRI) technique 
has received considerable attention globally including Tamil Nadu due to 
its potential for yield improvement and water saving. The main features 
of this system include transplanting of young seedlings singly in a 
square pattern with wide spacing; using more of organic fertilizers; and 
keeping the paddy soil moist with intermittent drying and wetting during 
the vegetative growth phase. SRI causes better plant growth and 
development and economizes upon the use of seed, irrigation water, 
labour, plant protection chemicals and fertilizers and hence increases 
the productivity of land, water capital and labour significantly over 
conventional flooded rice cultivation.

(c) whether Government has made any assessment regarding grant of 
subsidy to the farmers on the basis of the size of their land holding;

(e) whether Government proposes to rationalize subsidies in the 
agricultural sector; and

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI KANTILAL 
BHURIA): (a) and (b) The various kinds of subsidies being provided by the 
Central Government to the Agricultural Sector include subsidies on 
Fertilizers, Seeds, Micro I rrigation System, Machinery, Premium on crop 
insurance etc. The Government also provides financial 
incentive/grants/concession under various on- going Central Sector/ 
Centrally Sponsored Schemes namely National Food Security Mission (NFSM), 
Rastriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY), Macro Management, National 
Horticulture Mission, Technology Mission for Horticulture for the North 
Eastern States, etc. The allocations/releases to State Governments/UTs 
under these important programmes are given in the S tatement-I to V (S ee 
below). Fertilizer subsidy is provided to the Manufacturers/Importers, 
the benefit of which goes to the farmers through the notified selling

Suicide by farmers 
12. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA BHARTIA: Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether the exact reasons have been identified for the spate of 
suicide by farmers in the country; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the view of experts/NGOs in identifying the exact cause of 
suicide by farmers have been taken note of; 
(d) if so, whether any new study would be conducted to ascertain the 
exact cause of spate of suicide by farmers in the country; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI KANTILAL 
BHURIA): (a) to (e) The suicides by farmers have been reported from the 
States of Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Karnataka and Gujarat only in 
2008-09. The State Governments have broadly reported crop failure, 
indebtedness, drought, social and economic insecurities as causes for 
suicides by farmers, as also identified in various study reports in this 
context e.g. Tata Institute of Social Sciences (TISS), Indira Gandhi 
Institute of Development Research (IGIDR), Mumbai, National Institutes 
for Rural Development (NIRD), National Institute of Agricultural 
Extension & Management (MANAGE), Hyderabad and Veeresh Committee etc. 
Further, the Veeresh Committee in context of farmers' suicides in 
Karnataka has stated that connecting the incidents of suicides directly 
to any single cause would be erroneous, since it is a personal decision 
of the victim and the post suicide search for causes gives only 
circumstantial evidence.

New food policy 
†15. SHRI JAI PARKASH AGGARWAL: Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government proposes to formulate a comprehensive food 
policy in view of instability in the production of foodgrains, pulses and 
sugar; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) by when the new food policy is likely to be formulated? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI KANTILAL 
BHURIA): (a) to (c) There is no proposal under consideration to formulate 
a new food policy. The production of foodgrains, pulses and sugar during 
the last three financial years indicates a steady increase and as per the 
Fourth Advance Estimates for the year 2007- 08, the production of 
foodgrains and pulses is at an all- time record. However, the Government 
already has a comprehensive food policy under which Minimum Support Price 
(MSP) operations are carried out by the Government agencies in districts 
all over the country where there is marketable surplus of foodgrains. 
Farmers have the option to sell their produce at MSP or in the open 
market, as is advantageous to them. This policy ensures that farmers get 
remunerative prices for their produce. This also enables the Government 
to procure foodgrains for servicing the Targeted Public Distribution 
System and welfare schemes. Maintenance of a buffer stock of foodgrains 
to ensure food security is also one of the important objectives of the 
food policy. Further, the Government has launched the 'National Food 
Security Mission' with the aim of increasing production of wheat, rice 
and pulses through area expansion and productivity enhancement; restoring 
soil fertility and productivity; creating employment opportunities and 
enhancing farm- level economy to restore confidence of farmers. The 
Mission is presently being implemented in 312 identified districts of 17 
States of the country.

Rice varieties with more arsenic 
22. SHRI N.K. SINGH: Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that CSIR has found some rice varieties which 
accumulate much more arsenic from the soil with the result that their 
consumption is dangerous for human health; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) whether any steps are contemplated to counter the arsenic effect? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI KANTILAL 
BHURIA): (a) and (b) The studies conducted by National Botanical Research 
Institute, Lucknow under Council of Scientific and Industrial Research 
(CSIR) have found rice germplasms such as BRG- 12, BRG- 15 and BRG- 20 
accumulating higher arsenic (range 1034 ug 2650 ug/kg grain rice). 
Certain rice germplasms accumulating lower arsenic level were also 
identified: CN-1646-2, CN-1646-5, Gotrabhog and Nayanmoni (range 78.65 ug 
to 112.26 fig/kg grain rice). 
(c) The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) had taken up 
research on mitigation options of arsenic problem in West Bengal. Growing 
various legumes and pulses need to be encouraged which require less 
ground water. There should be more use of organic and green manures that 
moderate arsenic toxicity in soil-plant system by forming oregano-arsenic 
complexes. The Blue Green Algae (BGA) having ability to decontaminate 
soils of arsenic should be introduced in the pad dy fields. To have more 
basic and strategic research in arsenic related problems in entire food 
chain, a project under National Agricultural Innovation Project (NAIP) 
involving six centres with Bidhan Chandra Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya 
(BCKVV), Mohanpur as lead centre has been initiated for a period of more 
than 5 years with a budget of Rs.6.24 crores.

Suspension of fertilizer production 
27. SHRI K. CHANDRAN PILLAI: Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND 
FERTILIZERS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that production of fertilizers has remained 
suspended in a number of fertilizer companies; 
(b) if so, the details thereof and the reasons therefor; 
(c) whether Government has taken/proposed to be taken measures to 
resume production of fertilizers in those companies; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS 
(SHRI B.K. HANDIQUE): (a) to (d) Production of some of the fertilizer 
companies viz. Rashtriya Chemicals Fertilizers Ltd. (RCF) Trombay- V, 
Southern Petrochemicals Industries Ltd. (SPIC) Tuticorin, Duncans 
Industries Ltd. (DIL) Kanpur and Tuticorin Alkali Chemicals and 
Fertilizer Ltd. (TAC) have remained suspended. There is no production of 
Ammonium Nitro Phosphate (ANP) 20:20:0 and Urea at RCF-Trombay-V unit due 
to an explosion at the Prilling Tower top and shortage of Associated Gas. 
Production of TAC was suspended mainly due to non availability of Carban-

155 
di-Oxide from their parent company (SPIC). The production of SPIC -
Tuticorin/ DIL-Kanpur was suspended due to working capital constraints. 

156 
In case of RCF, ANP plant is being revamped. The technology is being 
changed from Prilling to Granulation. The plant is scheduled to resume 
production from third quarter of 2009. Also, Urea plant shall be started 
after the availability of RIL KG Basin gas. As per present indications 
this will be tentatively available from April 2009. SPIC/DIL are expected 
to resume the production after the availability of working capital . The 
respective private units are expected to take their own commercial 
decision for resumption of production.

Re-opening of Talcher 
†30. SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN PANY: Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND 
FERTILIZERS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the closed units of Fertilizer Corporation of India Ltd. 
(FCIL) located at Talcher in Orissa is likely to be operationalized in 
near future; 
(b) if so, the concrete steps taken so far in this direction; and 
(c) by when the production work would be restarted in the unit of FCIL 
located at Talcher? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS 
(SHRI B.K. HANDIQUE): (a) to (c) Pursusant to decision taken by the 
Government on 12th April, 2007 to examine the feasibility of reviving the 
various closed units of FCIL and HFCL subject to the confirmed 
availability of gas, the techno- economic feasibility of revival of the 
various closed units was examined. It was found that except for the 
existing plant machinery, the basic infrastructure, viz. land, water, 
electricity, railway siding, silos etc. could be gainfully utilized for 
setting up of new brown field urea projects, subject to availability of 
natural gas. Keeping in view the above, the Government on 30.10.2008 
approved constitution of an Empowered Committee of Secretaries to look 
into all financial models for revival of each of the closed units along 
with their other linkages including gas. The Government has also accorded 
in principle approval for considering write- off of Government of India 
loans and interest liabilities of FCIL and HFCL. However, final decision 
on the waiver will be taken when fully tied- up proposals are received by 
the Government. Pursuant to the Government's decisions, the Empowered 
Committee of Secretaries (ECOS) has been constituted and all options for 
revival of the various closed units including the Talcher unit of FCIL, 
are being examined by the ECOS. As regards the commencement of production 
in Talcher plant of FCIL, it is not feasible to indicate a time frame at 
this stage.

Selling of PDS wheat and rice in open market 
31. DR. GYAN PRAKASH PILANIA: Will the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS, 
FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether during last three years, Rs. 31,585.98 crore worth of 
wheat and rice meant for PDS and during 2006 alone, Rs. 11336.98 crore 
worth of PDS foodgrains were sold into the market illegally; 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 

164 
(b) whether every year, India's poor are cheated out of 53.3 per cent 
of wheat and 39 per cent of rice meant for them; 
(c) if so, the details thereof indicating the States which are the 
worst affected; 
(d) the action taken against guilty; and 
(e) the corrective steps taken? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND 
PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (DR. AKHILESH PRASAD SINGH): (a) No Sir. This amount 
of illegal sale of TPDS foodgrains in open market was wrongly mentioned 
in a Press Report in the Times of India dated 17th September, 2007. This 
Press Report seems to have used some figures on diversion reported in the 
study conducted by ORG MARG. Report of ORG MARG study was received in 
2005. It covered data of 2003- 04 and 2004- 05. This report mentioned 
diversion of TPDS foodgrains in a number of States. However, the amount 
mentioned in the Press Report is incorrect. It seems to have used 
economic cost of foodgrains as the basis for calculation assuming that 
there has been no improvement in functioning of TPDS in subsequent years, 
which is factually not correct. 
(b) and (c) The Department of Food and Public Distribution got TPDS 
evaluated by ORG MARG. This evaluation covered the period of 2003- 04 and 
2004-05. The report received in 2005 mentioned diversion of 39% of rice 
and 53% of wheat under TPDS. The report mentioned that diversion was 
because of inclusion errors, leakages through ghost ration cards and 
pilferage during transportation and from Fair Price Shops. State- wise 
details of diversion reported by the evaluation study of ORG MARG are 
given in the S tatement (See below). These figures of diversion reported 
in the study report were contested by most of the State Governments. 
Also, diversion of rice and wheat from BPL to APL family does not mean 
loss of the foodgrains. It results in delivery of foodgrains to 
unintended category of beneficiaries. After this study, State and UT 
Governments have taken a number of steps to check leakages, diversions 
and minimize identification errors, because of which diversion and 
leakages have got reduced. 
(d) and (e) The following measures have been taken to strengthen the 
functioning of TPDS. 
(I) A nine-point action Plan is under implementation since July, 2006. As 

165 
a part of 9-Point Action Plan: 
 (i) 17 States have initiated computerization of TPDS transactions 
from their own resources. 
 (ii) 100.48 lakh bogus/ineligible ration cards eliminated in 14 
States. 
 (iii) Door delivery of foodgrains to FPS being done in 16 
States/UTs. 
 (iv) PRI's involved in vigilance committees and running of FPS in 24 
States/UTs. 
 (v) BPL lists are being displayed at FPS in 30 States/UTs. 
  (vi) Review of BPL/AAY list has been undertaken in 30 States. 
  (vii) District and FPS wise allocation of foodgrains put on 
website as  
 public scrutiny in 19 States. 
(II) The concurrent evaluation of TPDS has been taken up in 26 States and 
UTs. The report of this concurrent evaluation has been received for 
12 States. Compared to earlier findings of PEO and ORG MARG, these 
reports have revealed improvement in functioning of TPDS in many of 
these States. 
(III) A model Citizens' Charter was issued by the Central Government 
in 1997 and again in 2006 for adoption by the State Governments/UT 
Administrations. A revised Citizens' Charter has been issued in July, 
2007 for adoption and implementation by State/UT Governments for 
facilitating use by Citizens of provisions of Right to Information 
(RTI) Act, 2005 in relation to functioning of the TPDS. By now 16 
State/UT Governments have adopted it. 
(IV) In order to ensure increased transparency in functioning of FPSs, all 
State and UT Governments have been directed on 7th March, 2008 to 
introduce monthly certification by Village Panchayats/Vigilance 
Committee/Urban Local Bodies/Self Help Groups for delivery of 
foodgrains to ration card holders with effect from April, 2008. 
(V) As a part of a Plan Scheme on strengthening of TPDS, the Department 
sanctions training programmes to be taken up by State and UT 
Governments for TPDS functionaries and members of Vigilance 
Committees, etc. 
(VI) Digitization of PDS operations of National/State/District and Block 
levels all over the country is proposed to be taken up under a Plan 

166 
Scheme on computerization of TPDS during the 11th Plan Period. 
(VII) Introduction of Global Positioning System (GPS) has been taken 
up by Chhattisgarh, Tamil Nadu and Delhi Governments for tracking 
movement of vehicles carrying TPDS commodities on pilot basis to 
assess its effectiveness. 
(VIII) For greater public scrutiny of TPDS functioning through the 
provisions of the RTI Act, 2005, publicity-cum-awareness campaign on 
TPDS is being taken up as a part of the plan scheme on strengthening 
of TPDS.

Actual selling price of electronic/electrical items 
35. SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN: Will the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD 
AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government is aware that in case of certain 
electronic/electrical items, the actual selling prices are much below the 
MRP printed on the packs by the manufacturers; 
(b) the factual position in this regard and whether this practice does 
not defeat the objective of the law requiring the indication of MRP on 
the products; and 
(c) the Government's assessment of the problem, the remedial steps 
taken/proposed in this behalf alongwith the outcome thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND 
PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (SHRI TASLIMUDDIN): (a) to (c) The Government has not 

178 
received any specific complaint that certain electronic/electrical items 
are sold much below the Maximum Retail Price (MRP) declared on a package. 
The MRP declared on a package gives protection to consumer from being 
overcharged by the retailer in excess of the price declared by the 
manufacturers. The case for taking remedial measures will arise only if 
consumers are charged a price higher than MRP. Excise duty  under the 
Central Excise Act is based on MRP declared on a package for notified 
commodities.  

179 
Thus if a manufacturer declares a higher price as MRP he will also have 
to pay higher taxes; this act as a deterrent to declare higher prices. 
Apart from this competitive market forces also will encourage 
manufacturers not to declare unreasonably higher prices.

Statement 
Steps taken by Government to prevent loss of foodgrains stored in the 
warehouses. 
The steps taken by Government to prevent loss of foodgrains stored in 
the warehouses are as follows:- 
(i) Godowns/warehouses are constructed and maintained on scientific lines 
for storage of foodgrains. 
(ii) Regular prophylactic and curative treatment of foodgrains are carried 
out for the control of insect pests. 
(iii) Regular periodic inspections of the stocks by qualified and 
trained staff is carried out and immediate remedial measures are 
taken, if shortcomings are observed. 
(iv) The foodgrains are stored on elevated plinths using proper dunnage 
material in Cover and Plinth (CAP) storage. 
(v) Stocks of foodgrains are treated with malathion and deltamethrin as a 
preventive measures to arrest infestation on fortnightly and 
quarterly basis. 
(vi) Whenever, infestation is noticed stocks are fumigated with Aluminium 
Phosphide. 
(vii) The stocks are covered with specially fabricated low- density 
polythene covers and tied with nylon ropes. 
(viii) Pest control/rodent control measures are undertaken. 

182 
(ix) Procedure of "First in First Out (FIFO) to the extern possible is 
implemented so as to avoid longer retention of stocks". 
(x) Movement of stocks of foodgrains are undertaken by covered wagons, 
etc. 
(xi) Pre-monsoon fumigation are carried out. 
(xii) The quality control checks are carried out by FCI at 
Zonal/Regional level and closely monitored at the FCI Hqrs.

Misuse and malpractice of PDS articles 
40. DR. K. MALAISAMY: Will the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND 
PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state: 
(a) what are the extra measures taken in addition to the conventional 
system and procedure to correct and control the misuse and malpractice of 
PDS articles; 
(b) what are the major areas of misuse and malpractice and the major 
articles on which such malpractices have been in vogue; and 
(c) whether such practices have been due to system failure or human 
failure or both? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND 
PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (DR. AKHILESH PRASAD SINGH): (a) to (c) In order to 
maintain supplies and securing availability and distribution of essential 
commodities, Public Distribution System (Control) Order, 2001 was issued. 
The Department of Food and Public Distribution got TPDS evaluated by 
ORG MARG. This evaluation covered the period of 2003- 04 and 2004-05. The 
report received in 2005 mentioned diversion of 39% of rice and 53% of 
wheat under TPDS. The report mentioned that diversion was because of 
inclusion errors, leakages through ghost ration cards and pilferage 

186 
during transportation and from Fair Price Shops. 
To streamline functioning of TPDS, Government has taken a series of 
measures. Apart from regular monitoring and review with State/UT 
Governments, Government has been getting functioning of TPDS evaluated 
from time to time through independent agencies. To streamline functioning 
of TPDS, steps taken by Government are of four categories: 

187 
(i) For improving functioning of TPDS machinery, continuous reviews of 
lists of BPL and AAY families, door step delivery of foodgrains to 
fair price shops, timely availability of foodgrains at fair price 
shops and training of staff as well as vigilance committee members are 
being emphasized. 
(ii) For greater transparency in functioning of TPDS, display of lists 
of BPL and AAY families at fair price shops, display of allocated 
quantities on web sites, adoption and implementation of revised 
Citizens Charter, monthly certification of delivery of foodgrains to 
fair price shops and their distribution to ration card holders, and 
taking up publicity-cum-awareness campaign have been initiated. 
(iii) Improved vigilance at various levels and strict penal action 
against those involved in malpractices, including action against staff 
responsible for issuing ineligible ration cards and persons found in 
possession of such ration cards are being emphasized. 
(iv) Introduction of new technologies such as Computerization of TPDS 
operation at various levels, smart- card-based delivery of essential 
commodities, use of global positioning system on vehicles transporting 
TPDS commodities and bar coding of ration cards etc. is being piloted. 
As can be seen, required legal and institutional framework has been 
put in place. However, efficient operation of TPDS depends on capacity of 
the machinery managing it. Therefore, it may be stated that the 
deficiencies noticed in implementation of TPDS seem to be more because of 
shortcomings in the machinery.

Implementation of population control measures 
48. PROF. ALKA BALRAM KSHATRIYA: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND 
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state: 

202 
(a) whether according to the latest report published in regard to the 
National Family Health Survey- Ill, it has been revealed that the 
fertility / rates are higher in some States and the steps taken by 
Government to check population control have become ineffective; 
(b) if so, the facts and details thereof; and 
(c) whether Government proposes to ensure that population control 
measures are effectively implemented in the country? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE 
(SHRIMATI PANABAKA LAKSHMI): (a) to (c) The current fertility trend in 
India is faster than replacement (i.e. 2.1) in NFHS- III which is 2.7 
children per women. The State-wise breakup of fertility rate at or below 
the replacement level are as follows: 
• TFR below 2.1 children per women has been achieved in 10 states viz. 
Delhi, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Sikkim, Goa, Maharashtra, Andhra 
Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu. 
• States, which have TFR above 2.1 in descending order: Bihar, Uttar 
Pradesh, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Jharkhand, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, 
Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram, Manipur, Haryana, Chhattisgarh, 
Uttarakhand, Assam, Gujarat, Jammu and Kashmir, Orissa, West Bengal, 
Tripura. Bihar (with TFR of 4.0) and Uttar Pradesh (3.8), Rajasthan 
(3.2) and Madhya Pradesh (3.1) top the list among the States having 
high TFR. The TFR decreased steeply by the Household's wealth index 
from 3.9 children for women living in household in the lowest wealth 
quintile to 1.8 children for women living in household in the highest 
wealth quintile. Apart from income rural urban background education 
religion, caste/tribe socio- cultural set of preference for son has 
been found responsible for high fertility. 
The following steps have been taken by the Government to check 
population control: 
(i) National Family Planning Insurance Scheme has been started since 
Nov. 2005 to provide insurance cover to the sterilization acceptors 
for failures, complications and death and also provides indemnity 
insurance cover to doctors/health facilities. 
(ii) The revision of Compensation package in Sept, 2007 to compensate 
for loss of wages and also to provide compensation to providers of 
services. It also provided for partnerships with the non -  
governmental sector. 
(iii) Specific action points/strategies have been incorporated in the 
States Project Implementation Plans (PIPs) under National Rural Health 

203 
Mission (NRHM) every year to address the up- gradation of Family 
Planning Services and increase the number of providers. 
(iv) Promoting Acceptance of No Scalpel Vasectomy to ensure male 
participation. 
(v) Promoting IUD 380 A intensively as a spacing method because of its 
longevity of 10 years and advantages over other IUDs. 
(vi) Fixed day Fixed Place Family Planning Services round the year made 
possible on account of growing number of 24x7 PHCs and better 
functioning CHCs and other health facilities under NRHM. 

204 
In addition to the above steps taken, the Government has a dedicated 
programme to undertake research for development and evaluation of 
contraceptive technologies for both male and females. During the last 
three decades, Government has evaluated different types of Intrauterine 
devices, Oral Contraceptives, injectable and implantable contraceptives 
for their efficacy and acceptability. In order to help couples with a 
backup method to prevent unwanted pregnancy, the emergency contraceptives 
have been introduced which are very useful method for preventing 
unplanned and unintended pregnancies.

51. SHRI RAMDAS AGARWAL: 
 SHRI DARA SINGH:

(SHRIMATI PANABAKA LAKSHMI): (a) Sex ratio (number of females per 
thousand males) is one the most important indicator used for study of 
population characteristics. Declining trend in sex ratio has been a 
matter of concern for all in the country. 
Child Sex Ratio for the age group of 0- 6 years in 2001 is 927 girls 
per thousand boys against 945 recorded in 1991 Census. 
The Census 2001 figures further reveal that the Child Sex Ratio is 
comparatively lower in the affluent regions, i.e., Punjab (798), Haryana

207

vide their letter dated 5.12.2008, 125 cases were registered during,

Techniques (Regulation and Prevention of Misuse) Act, 1994, was brought 
into operation from 1st January, 1996. The Act has been  amended  to  
make  it more comprehensive. The amended Act, viz. "Pre-conception and 
Pre- 

208 
Natal Diagnostic Techniques (Prohibition of Sex Selection) Act, 1994", 
and Rules and Regulations framed thereunder came into force with effect

Government to improve the Child Sex Ratio in the Country are constitution 
of the Central Supervisory Board under the Chairmanship of Union Minister 
of Health & Family Welfare, constitution of the National Inspection & 
Monitoring Committee for undertaking field visits periodically across the 
country, and constitution of the National Support & Monitoring Cell for 
effective implementation of the Act, training of Judiciary, publication 
of Annual Reports, Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs), organising 
sensitisation workshops/seminars, launching of 'Save the Girl Child' 
campaign, seeking cooperation from the NGOs/religious leaders, etc..

Nursing Midwife (ANM) and Accredited Social Health Activist (ASHA.) are

of Child Sex Ratio, for expending on the identified awareness generation 
activities. 
4. On 2.10.2007, on the occasion of the Birth Anniversary of the

every district of the NCT of Delhi to generate awareness among the 
public. 
5. Further, the National Level Meeting on 'Save the Girl Child' held

All the State/UT Governments have been requested to replicate such a

Clinical trials in Andhra Pradesh 
53. SHRI M.V. MYSURA REDDY: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY 
WELFARE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that there is no monitoring mechanism at the 
Central or State level to oversee the clinical tests in the State of 
Andhra Pradesh; 
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; 
(c) whether it has come to the notice of his Ministry that in the name 
of bio- equivalance or bio- availability tests, the pharmaceutical 
companies are carrying out clinical tests on innocent people which are 
resulting in even death of some people in Andhra Pradesh; and 
(d) if so, what action his Ministry has taken on such pharma 
companies? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE 
(SHRIMATI PANABAKA LAKSHMI): (a) and (b) Regulation of clinical trials 
comes under the purview of Central Drugs Standard Control Organization 
(CDSCO), Dte. General of Health Services and monitoring mechanism exists 
at Central level. Guidelines and requirements for conducting clinical 
trials in the country are specified in Schedule- Y of Drugs and Cosmetics 
Rules, 1945 and it requires that the clinical trial is carried out as per 
Indian Good Clinical Practices (GCP) Guidelines issued by Dte. General of 
Health Services. 
Before conduct of clinical trial the investigator is also required to 
give undertaking that he will maintain adequate, accurate records and 
make those records available for audit / inspection (Oversee) by the 
sponsor, Ethics Committee, Regulatory Authority or their authorized 
representatives. 
As per clause 3.1.13 of Indian GCP guidelines the sponsor should 
ensure that clinical studies are adequately monitored and they must 
appoint adequately trained monitor to supervise the clinical trial. 

215 
Further, clause 3.1.14 of said guidelines requires that sponsor should 
perform audit as a part of Quality Assurance system. Auditor should 
document their observations which should be made available to the 
Regulatory Authorities when called for. 
(c) and (d) Bio- equivalence / Bio- availability studies of new drugs 
are permitted to be carried out in the country in accordance with the 
Drugs and Cosmetics Rules. The studies are required to be conducted as 
per the GCP guidelines. 

216 
There was a report of death of a subject who was involved in a 
Bioequivalence study in a centre in Hyderabad. As per the information 
received from the bioequivalence study centre, the subject was 
administered the first dose of a drug on 26 November 2008 and was 
discharged on 28 November 2008. He submitted another blood sample on 29 
November 2008. As advised by the Centre the subject visited the center 
again on 5th December 2008 for second dosing planned on 6th December 2008 
and complained of chest pain and breathlessness. After preliminary 
treatment by the in house Doctor of the centre, the subject was shifted 
to nearby Hospital. As per the information received from the hospital 
cause of death could not be arrived as the patient was brought dead.

(SHRIMATI PANABAKA LAKSHMI): (a) to (e) UNFPA has been assisting the

assistance of US $ 341 million. The seventh Country Programme covering

219 
the implementation of phase-II of Reproductive and Child Health Programme

The RCH- II Programme had adopted an approach in which fertility 
reduction goes hand in hand with reduction in Maternal and Child 
Mortality. The current fertility trend of 2.7 children per woman in India 
in NFHS-III is faster than replacement rate of 2.1 children per women. 
The following steps have been taken by the Government to check 
population control:- 
(i) National Family Planning Insurance Scheme has been started since 
Nov, 2005 to provide insurance cover to the sterilization acceptors 
for failures, complications and death and also indemnity insurance 
cover to doctors/health facilities; 
(ii) The revision of comprehensive package in Sep. 2007 to compensate 
for loss of wages and also to provide compensation to providers of 
services. It also provides for partnerships with non- governmental 
sector; 
(iii) Specific action points/strategies have been incorporated in the 
States Projects Implementation Plans (PIPs) under National Rural 
Health Mission (NRHM) every year to address the up-gradation of Family 
Planning Services and increase the number of providers;

participation; 
(v) Promoting IUD 380 A intensively as a spacing method because of its 
longevity of 10 years and advantages of other IUDs; 
(vi) Fixed day Fixed Place Family Planning Services round the year made 
possible on account of growing number of 24x7 PHCs and better 
functioning CHCs and other health facilities under NHFIM. 
In addition, the Government has a dedicated programme to undertake 
research for development and evaluation of contraceptive technologies for 
both males and females. During the last three decades, Government has 
evaluated different types of Intrauterine devices, Oral Contraceptives, 
injectable and implantable contraceptives for their efficacy and 
acceptability. In order to help couples with a backup method to prevent 
unwanted pregnancy, the emergency contraceptives have been introduced

pregnancies.

Statement 
Details of the guidelines recently drafted by ICMR 
• Scope of Guidelines 
- These Guidelines apply to all clinical research whether sponsored by 
the Pharmaceutical or Medical Device Industry, Government or Academia 
or individual investigators. 
- These guidelines do not apply to Post Marketing Surveillance and 
ancillary care. 
• Basic Principles 
- Compensation be provided to the research participants when temporary 
or permanent injury occurs due to participation in the clinical 
research. 
- Compensation be paid to a child injured in- utero through the 
participation of the parent in clinical research. 
- Compensation be paid when injury is caused by a procedure which has 
been undertaken to manage an adverse reaction occurring during the 
research. 
- Compensation be paid irrespective of 
 - whether injury was foreseeable/predictable or not. 
 - The fact that the research participant had freely consented in 
writing to participate in the research. 
 - The fact that the injury was caused by the comparator product(s) 
under  
 investigation in the clinical research. 

241 
• Compensation be paid irrespective of the fact that the injury was 
caused through a departure from the agreed protocol, scientific 
misconduct or negligence by the Investigator. 
• Compensation may be excluded in light of factors described in Section 
5.4. 
• All research related injuries be compensated irrespective of their 
causes and individuals/agencies responsible.

82. SHRI M.V. MYSURA REDDY: Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased 
to state: 
(a) the details of the measures taken or proposed to be taken to 
strengthen the Railway Protection Force in view of the terrorist attack 
at Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminal; 
(b) whether there are any plans to increase the number of RPF 
battalions; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether it is not a fact that in view of the lack of proper 
training facilities to RPF personnel and also in the absence of having a 
special academy for providing modern security system, the security at 
railway station is not up to the mark; and 
(e) if so, the reasons why his Ministry cannot set up special 
academies in the country to train RPF and RPSF? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS (SHRI R. VELU): (a) 
Various measures have been taken to strengthen the Railway Protection 
Force. Important details are as under:- 
(i) An Integrated Security System is being installed at all Railway 
Stations of four Metro cities viz Chennai, Delhi, Kolkata and Mumbai and 
140 other vulnerable / sensitive stations of Indian Railways. This system 

261 
will comprise of the following broad areas:- 
1. Internet protocol based CCTV System with video analytics. 
2. Access control. 
3. Personal and baggage screening system. 

262 
4. Explosive detection and disposal system. 
Guidelines & technical specifications of equipment have been 
circulated to the General Managers of Indian Railways for implementing 
the project. 
(ii) On the recommendations of the Norms Committee, Rs. 60.76 crore has 
been sanctioned for procurement of security equipment to strengthen the 
Railway Protection Force (RPF). The Force is also being provided with 
modern automatic weapons like AK- 47 Riffes, INSAS 5.56 Rifles, Pistol 
Auto 9mm AI etc. Rs. 14.26 crore have been allocated for procurement of 
vehicles for RPF to improve mobility of the Force. 
(iii) Composite Security plan has been submitted by a Committee 
comprising of officers from Railways, RPF, IB, CISF, Delhi Police and 
NSG. This plan has been approved in principle. It is being implemented.

battalions of RPSF (Total 2217 posts in various Grades) against new 
assets without matching surrender. D&G (Direction & General) provision 
has been introduced in order to create workcharged posts for safe 
guarding Railway property and thwarting miscreant activities at remote 
project sites. Senior Administrative Grade level posts have already been 
created. 
(d) and (e) No, Sir. Jagjivan Ram Railway Protection Force Academy, 
Lucknow has been granted Central Training Institute status. Training 
modules have been standardized and upgraded for Zonal Training Centres of 
Railway Protection Force . Training for trainers programme has been 
organized in Bomb Detection & Disposal and in Disaster Management. 
Railway Protection Force personnel trained in these programmes will 
impart training to other Railway Protection Force personnel. Commando 
training is being organized at a large scale by getting slots in reputed 
training centres of other Para Military Forces. 
It has been decided to augment infrastructural facilities and 
equipment in the existing training centres of RPF. In phase- 1, following 
training centres have been selected for upgradation within a time frame 
of 2 years: 
1. Kharagpur (South Eastern Railway) 
2. Kimber Garden (Southern Railway) 
3. Bandikui (North Western Railway) 
4. Rajahi Camp, Goarakhpur (North Eastern Railway) 
5. Mokama, (East Central Railway)

Accident on Saryu Express 
†89. SHRI MOTTLAL VORA: Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether Government is aware that on 19th January, 2009, a large 
number of youth boarded the roofs of coaches because of non- availability 
of seats in Saryu Express and fifty youths fell down from the roofs at 
Chilbila station; 
(b) if so, the number of youth died and injured; 
(c) the aid extended by Government to the bereaved families of the 
dead and injured; 
(d) the reasons for not stopping the youth from boarding the roofs of 
the coaches; and 
(e) the steps being taken by Government to prevent such accidents in 
future? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS (SHRI R. VELU): (a) 
Yes, Sir. On 19.01.2009, some persons were found travelling on the roof 
of Train No.4125 (Saryu Express) at Pratapgarh Railway station and were 
brought down and accommodated inside the coaches by Railway Protection 
Force and Government Railway Police. On arrival of the train at Chilbila 
Railway station, few persons travelling unauthorizedely again boarded the 
roof of the train. Some of them fell down from the roof due to hit by 
branch of a tree near the track when the train was passing between 
Chilbila and Khandor Railway stations in Pratapgarh- Sultanpur section 
over Lucknow Division of Northern Railway. 
(b) 3 persons died and 28 were injured in this incident. 

283 
(c) No financial aid is permissible to the dependents of those dead 
and injured in this accident, as traveling on roof top of a train is 
unauthorized and is punishable offence under the provisions of the 
Railways Act, 1989. 
(d) Efforts were made to detrain the unauthorized roof travelers at 
Pratapgarh and Chilbila stations by Railway Protection Force Government 
Railway Police and station staff, but some of the youth climbed again on 
the roof of the compartment when train left from Chilbila, where there 
was no deployment of Railway Protection Force / Government Railway Police 
Staff. 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 

284 
(e) Following steps are being taken to prevent such incidents in 
future:- 
1. Frequent drives are being conducted by Railway Protection Force 
against roof travellers to prevent such incidents. 
2. Escorting staff are being briefed regularly to check such incidents 
during train escorting duty. 
3. Supervisory staff are also conducting frequent surprise checks to 
prevent such incidents. 
4. Action is being taken under section 156 of the Railways Act against 
the roof travellers. 
5. Security personnel have been advised to be more vigilant to prevent 
such incidents in future. 
6. Railway Protection Force, Government Railway Police and Commercial 
staff, where available, are advised not to allow any person to board 
on the roof of the train.

structurals by the steel producers, is determined by the demand of that

Shortage of water for agriculture 
105. SARDAR TARLOCHAN SINGH: Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) the water level in Punjab and Haryana and how much it is receding 
every year? Give the figure of last three years; 
(b) the steps being taken in this regard; and 
(c) how much is the shortage of water for agriculture in both the 
States? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI KANTILAL 
BHURIA): (a) The ground water level is being monitored by Central Ground 
Water Board (CGWB) - an organisation of Ministry of Water Resources. The 
position of water level and declining trend of water level as per the 
CGWB during the last three years in the State of Punjab and Haryana are:- 
Punjab - The depth of water level lies between 0.85 metre below ground 

305 
level (m bgl) in Muktsar and 31.32 m bgl in Fatehgarh districts during 
pre-monsoon (May) and during post- monsoon (November) varies from 0.84 m 
bgl in Muktsar district to 37.36 m bgl in Ludhiana districts. Very 
shallow water levels, < 2 m bgl i.e. water logging conditions are 
observed in parts of Ferozpur, Muktsar and in small patches in Gurdaspur 
and Rupnagar districts. Very deep water levels (>20 m) are observed in 
parts of Jalandhar, Kapurthala, Moga, Patiala, Sangrur, Nawanshahar and 
Amritsar districts. 
The trend of ground water level decline over last three years varies 
from less than 10 cm to more than 1 m per year in different parts of the 
State. The water level decline of more than 1 m per year has been 
observed at a few places in Fatehgarh, Gurdaspur, Hoshiarpur, Jalandhar, 
Kapurthala, Ludhiana, Nawanshahr, Patiala, and Sangrur districts. 
Haryana - The depth of water level during May varies from 0.35 m bgl 
in Gurgaon to 47.80 m bgl in Bhiwani district whereas the depth of water 
level during November varies from 0.42 m bgl to 57.10 m bgl in Gurgaon 
district. Water logging conditions are observed in the central part of 
the State covering parts of Bhiwani, Hissar, Jind, Jhajjar, Rohtak and 
Sonipat districts and in isolated patches in Gurgaon, Panipat and 
Yamunanagar districts. Very deep water levels (> 40 m) occur in Bhiwani 
district bordering Rajasthan. The trend of water level decline over last 
three years varies from less than 10 cm to more than 2 m per year in 
different parts of the State. Water level decline of more than 1 m per 
year has been observed at a few places in Ambala, Fatehabad, Gurgaon, 
Kaithal, Karnal, Kurukshetra, Panchkula, Panipat, Sirsa and Yamunanagar 
districts. 
(b) With a view to prevent water shortage, Government of Punjab has 
taken the steps like use of Laser Land Leveler, promulgation of 'The 
Punjab Preservation of Sub Soil Water Ordinance, 2008', diversification 
from Paddy to less water consuming crops, use of water saving techniques 
and capacity building & Training, etc. 
The Haryana Government has also taken steps like launching of Mass 
Awareness Programmes for conservation and judicious use of water, 
introduction of a scheme titled "Accelerated Recharge to Groundwater", 
provision of subsidy on adoption of Drip/Sprinkler System for irrigation 
to prevent over exploitation of groundwater, popularizing growing of less 
water intensive crops in the areas where water table is declining, etc. 
(c) As per information received from CGWB, Ground water is being over-

306 
exploited in both the States with rate of ground water development at 145 
% in Punjab and 109 % in Haryana. The Government of Haryana has reported 
that requirement of water for agriculture at 62% intensity is about 31.90 
Million Acre Feet (MAP), against the total availability from all 
resources of 18.75 MAF.

Brutal attack on Shri Yashwant Sinha, Member, Rajya Sabha 
THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION (SHRI JASWANT SINGH): Mr. Deputy 
Chairman, Sir, I  
had  earlier  thought  that whatever I have to say I would submit in 
Hindi. But in deference to my good  

328 
friend, the hon. Home Minister, who has very kindly stayed back, I will 
speak in English. I would submit that the issue that was raised earlier, 
just before the commencement of the Question Hour, by my distinguished 
colleague and Deputy Leader, Shrimati Sushma Swaraj, is a much larger 
issue than the bare skeletal facts of it that were cited by her. My 
esteemed colleague, who has formerly been the Minister of Finance, 
Minister of External Affairs, Leader of the Opposition in Bihar and 
member of this House also, and the former Chief Minister of Jharkhand, 
plus the leader of our party, have all been assaulted very badly. I do 
wish to submit that my friend, Shri Yashwant Sinha has suffered a 
grievous injury. His ligament has been broken and he cannot walk. The 
security that was provided to him received a blow on his head and had to 
undergo immediate medical attention which required seven stitches, so I 
am told. For almost 45 minutes, a senior Member of Parliament, was taken 
around the city in the back of a truck, where he had been 
unceremoniously, I dare not use the word, dumped, for what else can I 
say? No warrant of arrest was produced; no arrest was announced and yet 
he was arrested. I do not know if a report from the Government of 
Jharkhand has been received by the Parliament for the arrest of Shri 
Yashwant Sinha, or his subsequent release and what he was arrested for. 
It was a perfectly legitimate protest that the party had organised for 
what is going on in Jharkhand. I don't think it is simply a BJP issue or 
a Jharkhand issue or a party issue. There is a larger issue involved o f 
the privilege, prestige and standing of not just a senior Member of the 
House but indeed of the entire House itself. These are all, to my mind, 
not just disturbing but actually a perilous indication of where, we as 
the Republic, are heading. I appeal to you to let us know whether you 
have received, even now, any information in this regard, which is indeed 
an obligation on the part of the Government of Jharkhand to provide you. 
I would like to know whether you have any information about the medical 
report of a very senior Member of our House, whether you have received 
any report about this from the Government of India. I say, 'the 
Government of India', because the State is under President's rule; there 
is no elected Government there. Therefore, the Union Home Minister has a 
role to play, and that is why, he was urged to stay back, not for any 
other reason, but we expect that as a committed Union Home Minister, he 
will be able to inform us of what is happening in Jharkhand. It is a kind 
of mindless lawlessness which seems to have seized the entire State of 

329 
Jharkhand. It is a very worrisome situation because that State has also 
got a condition of near uncontrolled Maoists' attacks and Naxalite 
attacks on the institutions of State. Parliament is an institution, and 
Members of Parliament are representatives of that institution. You, Sir, 
collectively hold the prestige of each individual Member. Now, not only 
because he is a Member of my party but also being a colleague of many 
years of standing, as Leader of the Opposition, I consider it my bounden 
duty to appeal to you to inform us of the facts and also inform us as to 
what steps you intend taking on this matter. I also urge and request the 
Union Home Minister to inform us as to what steps the Government intend 
taking.

Liberalization of F.D.I. Guidelines 
SHRI MOINUL HASSAN (West Bengal): Sir, the Congress Government has 
taken an outrageous step in liberalizing the Foreign Direct Investment 
guidelines. At one stroke, across the board,  
the  sectoral  caps  on  FDI  have  been  nullified  by  excluding  
investments by companies "owned or  

348 
controlled" by Indians having substantial foreign capital. By this 
redefinition, FDI can be routed through "Indian companies" and not be 
classified as FDI. 
By this sleigh of hand, there will be no sectoral cap on FDI in 
telecom, Defence, aviation, media, etc. Even in the retail sector, FDI 
can make a backdoor entry through these guidelines. In the insurance 
sector, the present cap of 26 per cent can be subverted. This is a device 
to bypass Parliament where a legislation to amend the law to increase the 
cap in insurance is pending. 
While doing this, at the end of the present Government's tenure, the 
Government would like to ensure backdoor entry of FDI virtually in all 
sectors without limits. 
In view of this, I would say that the Government has shown its utter 
contempt for Parliament by announcing these new guidelines on the eve of 
the Parliament Session. Sir, it is nothing but they are bent upon eroding 
the economic sovereignty of the country. So, in this perspective, I would 
like to demand the rescinding of new guidelines immediately.

SHRI N. BALAGANGA (Tamil Nadu): The Government has issued the draft 
Coastal Management Zone (CMS) Notification 2008 on 1st May 2008 and, 
again, on 21st July 2008. The present Notification 2008 intends to 
replace the existing Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) Notification of 
February, 1991 that has already been amended 19 times in the past 17 
years and replace it with the new one to manage the country's 7,500 km 
long coastline. The proposed notification is being advocated without 
taking into account the livelihood issues of local people and it has 
already become contentious with fishing and coastal communities 
protesting the Government's move. With the Notification available only in 
English and Hindi, the communities living along the coast are not able to 
understand the draft. Since most people, especially the fishing 
communities cannot understand the contents of the document, there is a 
need to translate the draft CMZ notification into languages of the

out that the Government had not interacted with the local panchayats to 
spread awareness on the notification. They apprehend that the new zone 
classifications will pave the way for proliferation of Special Economic 
Zones, ports, tourist resorts, mining and similar other activities along 
large areas of the coast. I, therefore, request the Centre not to impose 
such a notification without consulting local authorities who would be 
directly affected and who would have to implement the guidelines on the 
ground. The basic purpose of notification of the CRZ 1991 did not serve 
well due to improper implementation. The implementation mechanism
